766830101.text: ...Terminal ballistics are impeccable, and the dispersion is close to the ideal.

766830102.text: According to our assessment models here at the Maison Gardiennage's weapons bureau, your weapon is very much a "cannon."

766830103.text: It's just a shame that we'd need at least two teams' worth of manpower to deploy your "musket" in the field. It's too complicated to use...

766830104.text: Thank you for the approval, Officer Chevreuse. Actually, I don't think the high barrier to entry's a bad thing. Before I had the "Soulsniper: Ritual Staff" custom-made by Xilonen, we agreed that...

766830105.text: "The stronger the weapon, the stricter its usage standards should be."

766830106.text: Apart from their difficulty of use, I've even considered placing a "moral cognition-based lock" on such weapons.

766830107.text: That way, we can ensure they are wielded by the right people, preventing any immense damage resulting from criminal theft.

766830108.text: That's a fair concern, Officer Chasca. Weapon theft that leads to committed crimes is not uncommon here in Fontaine.

766830110.text: Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage, Natlan's "Flower-Feather Clan"... and a Knight of Favonius? What's going on with this little gathering of yours?

766830113.text: #Bullseye. You caught on to the situation immediately, {NICKNAME}.

766830114.text: Some time back, the Special Patrol sent Turenna to Liyue to take part in a joint wargame. That wargame became the catalyst for ever more frequent exchanges between the armed forces of various nations.

766830115.text: This time around, it's the routine "Ballistic Wargame" between Fontaine and Mondstadt — aimed at sharpening combatants' battlefield-planning capabilities on all sides.

766830116.text: And this time, thanks to our friends in the Knights of Favonius putting in a good word, the warriors of Natlan's "Flower-Feather Clan" have joined the wargame as well.

766830117.text: The Flower-Feather Clan warriors are skilled at firing while in flight — they've opened the doors to a whole new world for us!

766830118.text: Hmm... The Knights must have gotten to know the Natlanese warriors during their expedition, then? Paimon should've thought of that sooner!

766830119.text: But what's a "Ballistic Wargame," really? Paimon understands every word individually, but put them together and it gets a little confusing...

766830120.text: Doesn't shooting just mean firing the gun and being done with it?

766830121.text: Are bullets allowed in wargames too?

766830122.text: Aha, if everyone had unlimited ammunition, you'd just hold down the trigger, and most enemies would be no problem at all.

766830123.text: But combat is a long-drawn-out process. A shooter can only carry so much ammunition, so every shot needs to land — and to land strategically.

766830124.text: So the Knights of Favonius have developed a new type of grenade to help shooters sharpen their understanding. The principle behind it is a little complicated, though...

766830125.text: As for the specifics, I'll let our friend from the Knights of Favonius walk you through it.

766830126.text: #Coming, coming — apologies! I was buried in report-organizing and hadn't even noticed the Honorary Knight and {M#his}{F#her} little white companion. My greetings to you both!

766830127.text: I'm Hedwig, member of the Knights of Favonius's General Affairs Company. I'm in charge of recording proceedings for this wargame, and coordinating between the gunsmiths and our other allies...

766830128.text: Speaking of which — the device for this round actually has a connection to you two. Do you remember the strange Samachurl statue that once appeared in Dadaupa Gorge?

766830130.text: Don't remember. Doesn't matter, does it?

766830131.text: Even Paimon's a bit fuzzy on it. Hedwig, why don't you give us the short version?

766830132.text: Right then. I'll skip past the old legends and the scattered intel and cut to it —

766830133.text: According to the Investigation Company's findings, that statue was the work of an ancient Samachurl. The "Ladler of Broth" Churldric had taken an unused Domain and reshaped it into a place to drill his battle formations.

766830134.text: The Honorary Knight defeated one of Churldric's lingering shadows back then, which caused the Domain to collapse — and the "Eyes of Upano" that oversaw the formations scattered out into the open.

766830135.text: Once the Support Company had a sample in hand, they spent the better part of a year carefully disassembling and analyzing it. Eventually they got the technology figured out, combined it with the design principles of Liyue's overhead surveillance devices...

766830136.text: ...And produced a kind of visualizing "observation grenade" — meant for long-range reconnaissance, so a shooter can gather information from a position of safety.

766830137.text: What a roundabout journey... Paimon never imagined that little fellow we wrapped up without much fanfare would leave behind such a mysterious treasure!

766830138.text: The upshot is, in a wargame setting, the "observation grenade" lets shooters see through the eyes of the round in flight — deepening their grasp of trajectory and obstacles...

766830139.text: ...So they can practice shooting strategies geared toward different scenarios. It works on quite a few clever little angles!

766830140.text: As for us Flower-Feather Clan members, our Saurian-riders often have difficulty determining the effects of shots we make while riding our Qucusaurs. We are up in the sky, after all, with our targets being far away...

766830141.text: These observation grenades can thus help us conduct battlefield damage assessments... That's a term I learned from the Special Patrol, by the by — it's a very concise concept.

766830144.text: At present, the people involved in the wargame have completed everything our two leaders, Chasca and Chevreuse, have designated for them.

766830145.text: All that's left is to complete our wargame with an expanded sample.

766830146.text: Since you're here, Honorary Knight, would you like to try it out?

766830148.text: I did notice during the Fontinalia Film Festival that you're quite a crack shot, and an inspired one, too.

766830150.text: #I'm personally interested to see how much your marksmanship's improved over the years, {NICKNAME}.

766830151.text: And from the perspective of the wargame, your lack of familiarity with the observation grenades means that you can form an excellent control group for us.

766830152.text: #Heh. Y'know, {NICKNAME}... It does feel like this grenade thing has real history with us.

766830153.text: Might as well try its effects for ourselves, eh? It should be pretty fun!
